main_body: A pew seen from the side (end-on): a tall brown backrest strip on the left with a seat section to its right containing red cushion panels stacked vertically
top_band: Seat region has only a thin 2-row orange-brown strip at rows ~14-15 on top; the backrest top (rows 8-10) is a 1-2px dark cap. No real horizontal surface visible from above.
evidence: Reading a column through the seat body (x~14-17): a 2-row lighter orange strip at rows 14-15, then the red cushion panels (rows 16-27, 30-41, 44-55) with dark red shadow at the bottom of each, separated by thin brown bars. The red areas are vertical faces seen face-on, like cushions drawn in elevation. The left backrest strip is a flat tall plank in profile. There is no seat surface visible from above; the 2px band is a rim, not a surface. This matches the side-elevation chair and thin seat failure patterns.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown, tinted to match the wood, which is good. But the red cushions are large flat fills of one red with only a dark-red shadow edge, and the wooden backrest plank is a flat brown with a single highlight column. Only about 3 steps per material, no grain or texture dots. Much sparser than the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and per-element texture.
